data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The claim that decentralized networks are more resilient is false; a large service with strict internal redundancy is superior because it can implement 'active isolation' and global load-shedding to halt correlated cascades.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The centralized coordination mechanism itself becomes the single point of failure (the 'Resilience Paradox').","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The failure mode is a 'poison pill' request that bypasses load-balancers and crashes every redundant node identically.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Centralized control allows for the immediate detection of a correlation pattern and the subsequent execution of a global 'kill switch' or traffic rerouting strategy. A decentralized network lacks the coordination mechanism to recognize a correlated failure in real-time, meaning each small service will continue to attempt (and fail) its operations, potentially exacerbating the failure through uncoordinated retries. The 'redundancy' in a large service is not just about copies, but about the ability to orchestrate the state of those copies globally.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
